auth.name: Authorization
auth.notes: Optional at the protocol level: the runtime mode depends on the server configuration (docs/rbac.md). JWT mode — when auth.jwt_secret / BPM_AUTH__JWT_SECRET is set, /api/v1 requests must carry "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" (HS256, claims {sub: actor, tenant, role, exp}); signature/expiry/claims are verified, failures answer 401 "invalid_token", and the verified claims drive tenancy and the roles matrix (403 "forbidden"). The tenant comes FROM THE CLAIM — the X-Tenant-Id header is deprecated in this mode and a header conflicting with the claim is rejected with 403 "forbidden". API-key mode — X-API-Key (auth.api_key / BPM_API_KEY) is the legacy admin/bootstrap credential with FULL access (no role checks) and X-Tenant-Id honored as untrusted input; a missing or invalid key answers 401 "unauthorized". When both are configured, a presented JWT takes precedence (the API key is the fallback when no bearer token is sent). Open mode — with neither configured every request is accepted (PoC) and X-Tenant-Id remains a dev-mode affordance. Tools with auth_required=false (health, readiness, capabilities) sit outside the auth layer entirely. Mint tokens with: cargo run -p bpm-engine-server-rest --example mint_jwt -- --sub <actor> --tenant <tenant> --role <role>.

conventions.classification: read_only — GET operations, plus the two POST endpoints validate and dry-run: they compile/simulate in memory and persist nothing (no definition, instance, task, timer, or history record; E2-2), so an agent may call them freely while exploring. mutating — every other POST/PUT/DELETE; consult the tool's side_effects note before calling. Replay-session operations are mutating but ephemeral: sessions live in memory and expire on inactivity, and no engine state changes.
conventions.error_shape: Every 4xx/5xx response body is {"error": <human-readable message>, "code": <stable snake_case identifier>, "invariant_violation": <invariant kind>} — the last field appears only on invariant-violation rejections and is mirrored in the X-Invariant-Violation response header. Codes are stable identifiers: adding one is backward compatible, renaming or removing one is breaking. One exception: a 400 from deploy carries the DeployError shape ({"error": ...} on a parse failure, {"errors": [...]} on compile failures) without a code field. Each tool's errors array lists the codes the operation's referenced response components document (a superset of what a specific call can trigger — the 400 component lists every boundary code); error_examples maps every code to a realistic example body.
conventions.pagination: GET /api/v1/process-instances pushes limit (1..=500, default 50) and offset (>= 0, default 0) into the store (SQL LIMIT/OFFSET in postgres mode) and returns a pagination object {limit, offset, returned}; out-of-range values are rejected with 400 "invalid_request". GET /api/v1/tasks and GET /api/v1/dead-letters accept the same optional parameters but slice in memory (dead-letter pages cap at the 100 entries the store returns per request); GET /api/v1/process-instances/{id}/history accepts an optional limit (1..=500) applied after sorting.
conventions.idempotency: POST /api/v1/process-instances accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header (1-128 printable ASCII bytes), scoped by X-Tenant-Id (bounded to 128 printable ASCII bytes when a key is supplied): a key already recorded for the tenant replays the recorded instance with 200 instead of creating a second one (201). The check-then-create sequence is single-service, not cross-process atomic — a key-recording failure after creation returns 500 "internal" with an explicit message, and retrying may create a second instance. No other operation consumes idempotency keys.
conventions.roles: E5-1 role→permission matrix, enforced for JWT-authenticated requests only (the admin API key bypasses role checks; open mode has no credentials to authorize). Roles: deployer — deploy, activate, deprecate process definitions; operator — start instances, complete user tasks, replay sessions, requeue/delete dead letters; worker — external-task fetch-and-lock, complete, fail, extend-lock (worker ONLY: the lease lifecycle belongs to the worker role; operators administrate via the DLQ); auditor — the read-only role. READS (every GET, plus the side-effect-free POSTs validate and dry-run) are allowed for ALL authenticated roles — cross-tenant reads are rejected by tenancy (404 "not_found"), not by role. A role without permission for an operation answers 403 "forbidden". All store queries are scoped by the VERIFIED tenant claim: lists are filtered to the tenant, instance/task/DLQ access of another tenant answers 404 (indistinguishable from unknown ids), and worker fetch-and-lock delivers only the claim tenant's tasks. Definitions are engine-global in v1 (readable by every tenant; only deployers modify them). See docs/rbac.md.

tools.name: list_dead_letters
tools.description:
Failed external tasks after retry exhaustion. Optional E2-4
route-level pagination (`limit` 1..=500, `offset` >= 0, else 400
`invalid_request`) slices the fetched entries in memory; absent
parameters keep the previous behavior. The fetch itself is
bounded: the store returns AT MOST 100 entries per request (both
the memory and Postgres adapters), so a page can never expose
more than the first 100 dead letters; deeper listing requires
store-level pagination (not part of v1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1..=500; default 50 on the instances list). Validated as 400 `invalid_request` when out of range. On `/dead-letters` the page is a window over at most the 100 entries the store returns per request (see that endpoint's description).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first returned entry (non-negative; validated as 400 `invalid_request` when negative).

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted
client input that scopes listings and instance starts (dev-mode
affordance).

tools.name: get_dead_letter
tools.summary: Get a single dead letter entry

tools.name: requeue_dead_letter
tools.summary: Requeue a dead letter entry as a new external task
tools.side_effects: Creates a new external task from the dead-letter entry and removes the dead-letter entry.

success.description: Entry requeued; the new task id is returned.

tools.name: fetch_and_lock_external_tasks
tools.summary: Fetch and lock external tasks for a worker
tools.description:
Lease-based delivery: one owner at a time, expired leases are
reclaimed first, tasks are ordered by creation time. Emits an
`ExternalTaskLocked` history event per delivered task.
tools.side_effects: Persists a lease per delivered task (one owner until the lock expires) and records ExternalTaskLocked history.

tools.name: complete_external_task
tools.description:
The worker returns result variables; the engine merges them and
advances the token via `ExternalTaskCompleted`. The E2-3
variable contract runs BEFORE the store mutates the task, so a
rejected request leaves the task locked and completable.

E3-1: an optional typed `envelope` field is validated
(4xx `task_envelope_invalid` with the sub-code in the message)
and merged into the reserved `__task_envelope` variable of the
merged map. The worker-sdk wire format (a serialized envelope at
that reserved key) is accepted; junk there, or supplying both
channels, is rejected with 4xx `reserved_variable_key`.
tools.side_effects: Emits ExternalTaskCompleted: merges the worker variables, closes the task, and advances the token; persisted with history.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted
client input that scopes listings and instance starts (dev-mode
affordance).

tools.name: extend_external_task_lock
tools.summary: Extend the lock duration of a locked task
tools.description:
Refused with 409 `lock_conflict` when the task is unknown, not
locked, or owned by a different worker.
tools.side_effects: Extends the persisted lease deadline of the locked task.

tools.name: fail_external_task
tools.description:
Decrements retries; at zero retries the task moves to Failed and
is enqueued to the dead letter queue, with a `TokenFailed` event.
E3-2 structured failure: optional `category`
(`transient`|`permanent`, else 400 `invalid_retry_category`):
`permanent` is BEHAVIORAL — the task skips the retry loop and goes
straight to Failed (DLQ + `TokenFailed`, exactly like retry
exhaustion; no redelivery). `transient` (or absent) keeps the
legacy decrement-and-requeue behavior. The category is also
recorded for observability (structured `error_message` prefix,
`envelope`, history, DLQ).
tools.side_effects: Decrements retries and requeues the task (transient), or at zero retries / permanent category moves it to Failed with a dead-letter entry and TokenFailed.

tools.name: check_invariants
tools.description:
Verifies the formal invariants (docs/invariants.md) over stored
instances/tokens/tasks/timers. Use for health checks, debugging,
or post-crash recovery verification.

tools.name: get_active_definition
tools.summary: Get the active version of a definition key

tools.name: deploy_process_definition
tools.summary: Deploy a process definition from BPMN 2.0 XML
tools.description:
Request body is the raw BPMN 2.0 XML document (content type
`application/xml`). Parse failures return 400 with the
`DeployError` shape carrying `error`; semantic compile failures
return 400 with the `DeployError` shape carrying `errors`;
persistence failures return 500 with the standard ErrorResponse
shape and code `deploy_failed` (E2-4 — previously persistence
failures reused the parse shape).
tools.side_effects: Persists a new immutable definition version (deploy never overwrites an existing version).

errors.description: Parse error (single message) or compile errors (list).

tools.name: dry_run_process_definition
tools.description:
Validate plus a dry-run walk with hypothetical start variables.
MUST NOT deploy and MUST NOT create any instance, task, timer or
history record. Same response contract as validate plus the
`dry_run` walk report.
tools.side_effects: None: compiles and simulates the walk in memory; no definition, instance, task, timer, or history record is created (classified read_only — see conventions.classification).

success.description: Validation outcome plus the walk report.

tools.name: validate_process_definition
tools.description:
Compiles the source and runs `validate_definition` WITHOUT
deploying. Compile errors are returned as HTTP 200 data
(`valid: false` + `compile_errors`); a successful compile reports
findings and `valid` is true when no finding is Critical.
4xx is reserved for malformed envelopes (`invalid_format`,
`empty_source`, `invalid_request_body`).
tools.side_effects: None: compiles the source in memory; nothing is persisted (classified read_only — see conventions.classification).

success.description: Validation outcome (compile errors and/or findings as data).

tools.name: list_definition_versions
tools.summary: List all versions of a definition key (newest first)

success.description: Versions for the key (empty when unknown).

tools.name: get_process_definition_view
tools.summary: Definition view (nodes and edges) for the Trace UI diagram

tools.name: activate_definition
tools.summary: Set a version as the active one
tools.side_effects: Persists the active-version pointer of the definition key.

tools.name: deprecate_definition
tools.side_effects: Persists the deprecated status on the definition version.

tools.name: list_process_instances
tools.description:
One page of process instances visible to the tenant, ordered by
instance id. The window is pushed into the store (SQL
LIMIT/OFFSET in postgres mode) — this is the hot path.

`limit` defaults to 50 and must be in 1..=500; `offset` defaults
to 0 and must be a non-negative integer; malformed or
out-of-range values are rejected with 400 `invalid_request`. An
offset beyond the end returns an empty page with
`pagination.returned = 0`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1..=500; default 50 on the instances list). Validated as 400 `invalid_request` when out of range. On `/dead-letters` the page is a window over at most the 100 entries the store returns per request (see that endpoint's description).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first returned entry (non-negative; validated as 400 `invalid_request` when negative).

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted
client input that scopes listings and instance starts (dev-mode
affordance).

success.description: Page of instances (the `pagination` field is additive, E2-4).

tools.name: start_process_instance
tools.description:
Creates a process instance for the given definition and emits
`ProcessStarted` through the engine event loop.

With an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-128 printable ASCII bytes):
a key already recorded for the same tenant returns **200** with
the same `{instance_id, status}` shape for the originally created
instance (idempotent replay, no second instance); an unknown key
creates the instance (201) and records the mapping. Atomicity is
single-service: concurrent identical requests can still race, and
a key-recording failure after creation returns 500 `internal`
naming the situation.
tools.side_effects: Creates and persists a new process instance with its tokens and variables, and records ProcessStarted history; an Idempotency-Key replays the recorded instance instead of creating a second one.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Start-instance idempotency key (E2-4): 1-128 printable ASCII
bytes. A known key replays the recorded instance with 200;
unknown keys are recorded on creation. Malformed keys are
rejected with 400 `invalid_request`.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted
client input that scopes listings and instance starts (dev-mode
affordance).

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id

tools.name: get_instance_history
tools.description:
Events in causal order (by `occurred_at`, then `id`) with
zero-based `sequence` and `category` (`instance` | `token` |
`external`). Optional filters `token_id` and `event_type`; the
optional `limit` (1..=500, E2-4) truncates the returned list
after sorting. Absent parameters keep the pre-existing
full-history behavior.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional cap on the number of returned events (1..=500, validated as 400 `invalid_request` beyond).

parameters.name: token_id
parameters.description: Filter events for a single token.

tools.name: create_replay_session
tools.description:
Snapshots the instance's history into an ephemeral replay
session. Sessions are in-memory only and expire after inactivity
(docs/replay-rest-api.md; the Replay API may evolve —
docs/api-spec.md §8).
tools.side_effects: Ephemeral only: snapshots the instance history into an in-memory session that expires on inactivity; nothing is persisted and no engine state changes.

tools.name: get_instance_steps
tools.description:
One step per `(node_id, token_id)` in causal order (steps are
numbered from 1 in first-event order), joining token transitions,
worker lease attempts (`ExternalTaskLocked` →
`ExternalTaskCompleted`/`ExternalTaskFailed`; a re-lock of a task
with an unresolved attempt closes that attempt as `expired` —
E1-3 redelivery after lease expiry) and the E3-1 AI task
envelope metadata (model/tool versions, cost) keyed by the trace
id. Read-only aggregation over the instance, definition and
history stores — no new stores, no new event types. `trace_id` IS
the instance id in v1 (a dedicated OTel-style trace id is future
observability scope); per-HTTP correlation stays on the
`X-Request-Id` header. The pre-existing `/trace` graph endpoint is
unchanged.

Sensitive-by-default: the response carries NO variable values —
only event types/timestamps, worker ids, retry counters, variable
NAME lists (`variables_touched`), and envelope METADATA summaries;
redacted or unparsable envelopes degrade to `{"opaque": true}`.
A definition that is ABSENT only degrades step-kind
classification (event-type fallback); a definition that fails to
LOAD is a storage error and answers 500 `internal`.

success.description: The step timeline of the instance.

tools.name: get_instance_trace
tools.description:
Instance state plus token timelines and external-task history
aggregated by token/task, computed from history events. Shares
the History API semantics (docs/api-spec.md §9).

tools.name: delete_replay_session
tools.side_effects: Ephemeral only: drops the in-memory replay session; no persisted state changes.

success.description: Session destroyed (unknown ids are a no-op 204).

tools.name: replay_seek
tools.description: Re-applies events `[0..cursor]` and stores the snapshot.
tools.side_effects: Ephemeral only: moves the in-memory replay cursor; no persisted state changes.

success.description: Seek completed; snapshot at the new cursor.

tools.name: replay_step
tools.side_effects: Ephemeral only: advances the in-memory replay cursor; no persisted state changes.

success.description: One event applied; new snapshot returned.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description:
Waiting user/service/external tasks of running instances.
Optional `type` filter (`user` or `external`) and the E2-4
route-level pagination parameters `limit`/`offset` (validated
like the instances endpoint: `limit` 1..=500, `offset` >= 0, else
400 `invalid_request`), applied in memory over the full scan;
absent parameters keep the previous full-list behavior.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1..=500; default 50 on the instances list). Validated as 400 `invalid_request` when out of range. On `/dead-letters` the page is a window over at most the 100 entries the store returns per request (see that endpoint's description).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first returned entry (non-negative; validated as 400 `invalid_request` when negative).

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted

tools.name: complete_user_task
tools.description:
Emits `UserTaskCompleted` through the engine event loop. The
E2-3 variable value contract and required form fields are
enforced at this boundary; the reserved `__task_envelope` key is
rejected (E3-1, `reserved_variable_key`).
tools.side_effects: Emits UserTaskCompleted: merges the submitted variables into the instance and advances the token to the next node; both the state change and the history record are persisted.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Id
parameters.description:
Tenant scope for the request (optional). DEPRECATED for
JWT-authenticated requests (E5-1): the tenant comes from the
verified `tenant` claim, an absent or agreeing header is accepted,
and a CONFLICTING header is rejected with 403 `forbidden`. In open
and API-key modes the header keeps its pre-E5-1 meaning: untrusted
client input that scopes listings and instance starts (dev-mode
affordance).

tools.name: get_task_form
tools.summary: Form schema of a user task
tools.description: `task_id` has the form `<instance_id>:<node_id>`.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description:
Serves the committed agent tool catalog
(`crates/server/rest/capabilities/agent-tools.json`, embedded at
compile time — no runtime YAML parsing): one tool per operation
of this spec, with parameter schemas (flattened minimal JSON
Schemas), read_only/mutating classification, side-effect notes,
auth requirements, and per-code error examples. See
docs/agent-tools.md.

UNAUTHENTICATED by design, like `/health` and `/ready`: it is
discovery metadata for agents BEFORE they hold an API key, and
it carries no secrets — only route shapes and stable error
codes derived from this public spec. The engine operations
under `/api/v1` keep the API-key + rate-limit layers.

The consistency suite regenerates the catalog from this spec
and fails when the committed artifact drifts; regenerate with
`cargo run -p bpm-engine-server-rest --example dump_capabilities`.

tools.name: get_health
tools.description: Always returns 200 while the process is up.

tools.name: get_readiness
tools.description:
Checks the engine and the storage backend (plus the Postgres pool
and migration state in postgres mode). `status` is `ok` or
`degraded`; numeric check values are informational.
